Original Requirements: Build the Volopa OOP (Out-of-Pocket) Expenses API System using Laravel 10+ with PHP 8.2+. Three modules: 1. User Management & Permissions — RBAC via user_feature_permission with delegation hierarchy 2. Pocket Expense CSV Batch Upload — synchronous validation, async background sync 3. Single Expense Data Capturing — CRUD with FX conversion and flexible metadata
Product Goals: Enable seamless out-of-pocket expense tracking for employees using personal payment methods
Provide flexible permission delegation system allowing admins to manage expenses for their teams
Support efficient bulk expense entry through CSV upload with comprehensive validation
Deliver accurate multi-currency FX conversion with client commission application
Ensure secure role-based access control with audit trail for permission changes
Maintain data integrity through atomic operations and comprehensive validation
Provide clear error feedback and user guidance for failed operations
Enable configurable expense sources and metadata for client-specific requirements
User Stories: As a Primary Administrator, I want to manage all users' expenses and delegate permissions to reduce my workload bottleneck
As an Administrator, I want to manage expenses for users I've been granted access to, so I can support my team efficiently
As a Business User, I want to create and edit my own expenses with automatic FX conversion when using foreign currencies
As a Card User, I want to upload receipts and add metadata to my expenses for proper tracking and compliance
As an Admin with management rights, I want to bulk upload expenses via CSV for multiple users to handle historical data efficiently
As a Primary Admin, I want to grant and revoke management permissions to other users based on organizational changes
As any user, I want to see clear validation errors when my CSV upload fails, with downloadable error reports
As a user entering expenses, I want the system to auto-convert foreign currency amounts using current exchange rates
As an expense creator, I want to override FX conversion amounts when I have more accurate rates or specific requirements
As a client administrator, I want to configure custom expense sources beyond the default Cash/Corporate Card/Personal Card options
As a user, I want to receive notifications when batch uploads complete successfully or fail
As an approver, I want to review and approve expenses with full audit trail of who created and modified each entry
Competitive Analysis: Expensify: Strong mobile app with receipt OCR, but limited delegation features and complex pricing
Concur SAP: Enterprise-grade with deep integrations, but heavy UI and expensive for SMEs
Rydoo: European-focused with good multi-currency support, but lacks flexible permission delegation
Zoho Expense: Affordable with basic features, but limited customization and weak FX handling
Receipt Bank (Dext): Excellent receipt processing, but primarily focused on accounting firms rather than corporate expense management
Webexpenses: Good approval workflows, but dated UI and limited API capabilities
Chrome River: Strong compliance features, but complex setup and poor user experience

Requirement Analysis: The Volopa OOP Expenses system addresses three critical business needs: (1) Comprehensive expense tracking for out-of-pocket business costs, (2) Scalable permission management through delegation hierarchy, and (3) Efficient bulk data processing. The system must integrate with existing Volopa infrastructure including OAuth2 authentication, FX services, and wallet management. Key technical challenges include atomic CSV validation (all-or-nothing), real-time FX conversion with client-specific commission rates, and flexible metadata storage. The permission model requires careful implementation of role-based access with delegation capabilities that don't conflict with existing Volopa user roles. Security constraints mandate proper input validation, SQL injection prevention, and audit logging for permission changes.
Requirement Pool: Implement secure OAuth2-authenticated API endpoints for expense CRUD operations with role-based access control
Build atomic CSV batch upload with comprehensive validation and detailed error reporting
Create flexible permission delegation system allowing management rights assignment independent of user roles
Implement real-time FX conversion with 30-day lookback, client commission application, and user override capability
Design normalized database schema with proper relationships, indexes, and soft delete support
Build configurable expense source management with client-specific customization up to 20 sources
Implement comprehensive audit logging for permission grants/revokes and expense modifications
UI Design draft: The system is API-first without frontend UI requirements. API responses should follow RESTful conventions with consistent JSON formatting. Error responses must include detailed field-level validation messages with line numbers for CSV uploads. Success responses should use appropriate HTTP status codes (201 for creation, 204 for deletion, 422 for validation errors). The CSV template should be downloadable with clear column headers matching the validation requirements. API documentation should include examples for both single expense entry and batch upload scenarios. All endpoints require OAuth2 Bearer token authentication and return paginated results where applicable using Laravel's standard pagination format.
Anything UNCLEAR: Three unresolved decisions need clarification: (1) Notification channel preference for batch upload completion (in-app, email, or both), (2) Whether FX conversion should reuse existing platform services or requires new integration patterns, (3) Specific audit logging mechanism to use (Laravel activity log, event sourcing, or custom audit table). The relationship between 'oop_expenses' and 'pocket_expense' tables has been resolved - only pocket_expense should be implemented as it supersedes the earlier oop_expenses design. Table naming conventions need verification (singular vs plural) based on existing Volopa standards.
